news.title: Former England international thinks Argentina World Cup loss could open Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane
news.lede: Former England international Danny Mills believes Harry Kane deserves serious consideration in the Ballon d’Or conversation after another phenomenal year for club and country. “Looking at the Ballon d’Or, Harry Kane has probably been the most consistent player in football so far this year. He’s been phenomenal, but I don’t think there’s been one particularly shining light; it undoubtedly depends on who is voting. I’m sure even though the final didn’t go to plan, Lionel Messi will get a few votes,” Mills told talkSPORT Bet slots site.

news.title: World Cup red card 'troubled' Howard Webb as conspiracy theorists slammed
news.lede: Pro Ref (formerly PGMOL) chief Howard Webb insists he was left "really troubled" by the decision to overturn Folarin Balogun's World Cup red card following political interference. Webb, who is about to embark on his fifth season as Chief Refereeing Officer, notes the call has sparked unfair claims of widespread "corruption" - which he feels is incredibly dangerous for the game's image. The 55-year-old said: "I was really troubled by it, really. I don't know the ins and outs of the process, obviously, what happened in the end, but the fact that we know... well, what do we know?

news.title: Private Equity Is Buying Up the World of Football
news.lede: Football confederations revolted against Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup. But the failure of his scheme won’t affect the bigger picture as private-equity firms gobble up football clubs in pursuit of short-term gains. While football clubs are relatively high-risk assets, the willingness of fans to support their local teams will persist in spite of economic uncertainty. Private equity firms want to exploit this loyalty, and they’ve been investing heavily in the sport.

news.title: Azcárraga: ‘I don’t see a World Cup in Mexico in 2038 as a far-fetched idea’
news.lede: The 2026 World Cup, co-hosted by Mexico, Canada and the USA left a hugely positive lasting impression on everyone who attended matches in Mexico City, Guadalajara and Monterrey; indeed, many wondered why there were only a handful of matches played on Mexican soil. Amid such euphoria, fans wondered whether Mexico would ever host another football festival, and to everyone’s surprise, the prospect of another men’s tournament is not so far off. At an interview with TUDN, Emilio Azcárraga Jean, president of Club América and an influential figure in Mexican football with contacts within the FMF (Mexican FA), said that hosting another men’s World Cup on Mexican soil in 2038 is not far-fetched. With confederation rotation, the conditions could align within three cycles.

news.title: Fears World Cup row over Folarin Balogun could fuel Prem conspiracy theories
news.lede: REF chief Howard Webb fears the World Cup row over USA striker Folarin Balogun could fuel false PREM conspiracy theories. Pro Ref boss Webb admitted he was “troubled” after the intervention by US President Donald Trump saw Balogun cleared to play against Belgium despite his red card for serious foul play being confirmed. And the former whistler conceded his concerns that intervention in football governance by outside figures could convince some fans that the entire game is suspect. news.title: AFA president Claudio Tapia lashes out at Argentina’s World Cup final conspiracy theories
news.lede: A month after Argentina fell 1-0 to Spain in overtime at the 2026 World Cup final, Argentine Football Association (AFA) president Claudio Tapia broke his silence with a lengthy, pointed statement on social media, taking direct aim at what he called a “miserable campaign” to paint the national team as having thrown the match. The backlash stems from a wave of conspiracy theories that spread in Argentina in the weeks following the loss, some of them tied to a leaked video showing Lionel Messi delivering an unusually calm pre-match speech in the locker room, in which he told his teammates to “forget about everything”. That clip was seized on by some to suggest the players had mentally checked out before kickoff, and it wasn’t long before speculation grew into open accusations, with some in Argentina even floating the idea that the squad had deliberately “given away” the final.
